title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.0.1-rc.2
summary: First file-transfer replacement RC: visible progress and cancellation, paced streaming to reduce mouse contention, and collision-safe incoming files. Includes rc.1 hardening. Use this RC on both PCs; real hardware feedback is needed.
changes: Standard Windows progress window on both ends with bytes, speed, estimated time, and Cancel. Transfer I/O never synchronously updates this window.
Replaced the file copy loop with bounded 32 KiB streaming and 64-bit counters. The 100 MB clipboard-file restriction is removed.

A shared 2 MiB/s default file-traffic budget reduces bursts; the transfer window offers 10 MiB/s and unlimited modes. The default is a starting point for hardware testing, not a measured guarantee of lag-free input.
Cancellation interrupts the transfer socket. Incomplete destination files are discarded; successful duplicate names keep both files.
File sharing is checked at send/receive entry and during file streaming. Existing encrypted connections, single-EXE packaging, and mouse/keyboard protocol are retained.
testing: Exit both copies and back up the old EXE and prefs. Replace only the EXE on both PCs and confirm About shows 1.0.1-rc.2.
Copy a 200 MB or larger disposable file in each direction. Both ends should show progress, speed, remaining time, and Cancel. Confirm the destination opens and has the right size.

While copying, move the mouse, type, and drag windows on the other PC. Compare default Protect mouse against Faster/Maximum; tell us which mode remains comfortable on your Wi-Fi. The slower endpoint limits the transfer.
Cancel from the sending PC, then repeat and cancel from the receiving PC. The transfer should stop and the receiving folder should not contain a finished-looking partial file. Send again to retry.
Send two different files with the same name to the same destination. The original should survive and the second should receive a numbered name.
Disconnect Wi-Fi during a disposable transfer. Expect an interrupted status, not success on the receiver; restore Wi-Fi and send again.
Try an empty file and a file over 2 GB if available. Also recheck text/image clipboard, lock/unlock, sleep/wake, and reconnection.
known_limitations: This is the first replacement stage, not a complete new transport protocol. No pause/resume, one-click retry, end-to-end checksum receipt, folder transfer, or Explorer-window drop targeting yet.
Sender progress counts bytes written to the connection and explicitly says to check the receiving PC. Only the receiver can report that the destination was committed.
Pacing is a configurable fixed budget, not adaptive Wi-Fi QoS. Mouse improvement must be assessed on real PCs. Setting the receiver to a lower rate also limits the sender.
The existing single incoming-transfer gate remains; overlapping requests may be rejected. Broader legacy clipboard policy and IPC lifecycle audit follow-ups remain.
